qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c (764 lines) + qemu_plugin/Makefile. Do NOT review the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h. Look for dead drain paths, duplicated CSR-list iteration that should use the X-macro, stale comments about removed QEMU2 leg.

1	# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
2	# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
3	# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
4	#
5	# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
6	# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
7	# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
8	# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   make            # build both
12	#   make clean
13	#
14	# Output (in this directory):
15	#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
16	#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)
17	
18	CC ?= gcc
19	
20	GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
21	GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)
22	
23	CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
24	HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
25	# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
26	QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
27	INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
28	LDFLAGS := -shared
29	LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)
30	
31	.PHONY: all clean
32	
33	all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so
34	
35	libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
36	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
37	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
38	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
39	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
40		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)
41	
42	# hotIterationLoop is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not
43	# HYBRID_INCLUDE.
44	libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c
45		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)
46	
47	clean:
48		rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so

1	// Pattern recogniser for the magic handoff marker convention. The same
2	// predicate runs in two places: the QEMU TCG plugin (C) and the vsim PC
3	// pre-scan (C++).
4	//
5	// The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions: SLTI with rd=x0 discards its
6	// result, so it is an architectural NOP on every conforming core. Marker
7	// binaries therefore run unmodified on real silicon and on every engine
8	// (fast/cycle/hybrid) -- unlike the retired `csrwi 0x7C0` markers, where
9	// CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores and the exit marker enabled ILM at
10	// base 0, killing standalone runs. The 12-bit immediate carries the
11	// marker kind; rs1 is pinned to x0 so each marker is one exact 32-bit
12	// word. SLTI has no compressed form, so markers are always 4 bytes.
13	
14	#ifndef HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
15	#define HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
16	
17	#include <stdbool.h>
18	#include <stdint.h>
19	
20	#ifdef __cplusplus
21	extern "C" {
22	#endif
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_NONE  = 0,
27	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER = 1,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A0
28	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT  = 2,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A1
29	} hybrid_handoff_kind;
30	
31	// slti x0, x0, imm: OP-IMM (0x13), funct3=010, rd=rs1=x0, imm[31:20].
32	#define HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN 0x5A002013u
33	#define HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN  0x5A102013u
34	
35	// Returns true when `insn` is one of the two marker HINTs. On match,
36	// *out_kind is set to ENTER or EXIT.
37	static inline bool hybrid_match_handoff_insn(uint32_t insn,
38	                                             hybrid_handoff_kind* out_kind)
39	{
40	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN) {
41	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER;
42	    return true;
43	  }
44	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN) {
45	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT;
46	    return true;
47	  }
48	  return false;
49	}
50	
51	#ifdef __cplusplus
52	}  // extern "C"
53	#endif
54	
55	#endif  // HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H

2	// allocates one of these per matched insn during vcpu_tb_trans and forwards

4	// the PC at which vsim should resume (i.e. the architectural PC immediately
5	// after the trigger insn retires).
6	//
7	// This indirection exists because qemu_plugin_read_register("pc") inside an

findings.title: libhybrid_handoff.so prerequisite list omits 3 of the 6 hybrid headers the .c includes (and the vendored qemu-plugin.h)
findings.detail: hybrid_handoff.c lines 5-12 include hybrid/handoff_site.h, hybrid/insn_match.h, hybrid/reg_names.h, hybrid/state_abi.h, hybrid/v_drain_policy.h, hybrid/write_mask.h, and <qemu-plugin.h>. The Makefile rule (lines 35-39) lists only state_abi.h, state_abi_check.h, insn_match.h, write_mask.h. Missing: handoff_site.h, reg_names.h, v_drain_policy.h, and include/qemu-plugin.h (the Makefile header comment at lines 5-8 even says to re-copy qemu-plugin.h on an API bump, yet a re-copy does not trigger a rebuild). Editing v_drain_policy.h (the L11 drain-policy logic is a static inline in that header, per include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h) leaves a stale libhybrid_handoff.so - the exact stale-.o failure mode already recorded in the project memory note 'Pipe swallows build exit code'. The libhotIterationLoop.so rule (line 44) likewise omits its include/qemu-plugin.h dependency.
findings.safety: Adding prerequisites (or switching to -MMD/-MP auto-deps) changes only when make rebuilds, never what it builds; the compile command line is untouched, so the produced .so is byte-identical for a given source state.
findings.verify_with: make -C qemu_plugin from clean succeeds; touch include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h and confirm libhybrid_handoff.so rebuilds; then tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh.

findings.title: Header comment claims the register-name tables are used by vsim's gdbstub handback client - that consumer was removed with the QEMU2 leg
findings.detail: reg_names.h lines 1-3 say the tables are 'Used by the QEMU TCG plugin (C) at drain time and by vsim's gdbstub handback client (C++) at restore time.' CLAUDE.md states the QEMU2 handback leg was removed entirely. I grepped for hybrid_gpr_names/hybrid_fpr_names/reg_names across /home/nick/work/andesim (plugin + driver/) and /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim: the only consumers are qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c lines 7/180/181 and the ABI's own compile checks (include/tests/abi_compile_check.c/.cpp). No gdbstub handback client exists in the vsim repo's src/. Note this file lives in the include/ submodule (andesim_abi repo), so the fix is a submodule commit + pointer bump; the C++ extern-C guards can stay since the compile check builds it as C++.
findings.safety: Comment-only change; no token outside comments is touched, so the compiled plugin and the ABI compile checks are unaffected.
findings.verify_with: include/tests/check.sh (the ABI compile check) and make -C qemu_plugin still build; grep confirms consumers unchanged.

findings.title: Redundant memset(sp, 0, sizeof(*sp)) at the top of drain_state_into
findings.detail: drain_state_into zeroes the caller's output struct at line 321, then builds the entire state in a zero-initialized local (line 322: struct hybrid_state_v1 s = {0}) and unconditionally copies it out at line 473 (*sp = s) - the only paths that skip line 473 call exit(2) (lines 432, 495-499 are in callees that terminate the process), and the sole caller drain_state_to_file (line 508) reads the struct only after the call returns. hybrid_state_v1 is padding-free by design (include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h asserts every field offset), so the {0} local plus struct assignment already determines every output byte; the memset writes bytes that are always overwritten.
findings.safety: The memset's effect is fully shadowed by the unconditional *sp = s on every returning path; removing it cannot change any byte of the written state file.
findings.verify_with: tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh plus a hybrid e2e with --verify (scripts/run_e2e.sh FILTER=rt_csr), which byte-compares the drained state.

findings.title: Unused #include <fcntl.h>
findings.detail: Grep for fcntl.h symbols (open(, O_WRONLY, O_CREAT, O_EXCL, O_RDONLY, fcntl, F_*) in hybrid_handoff.c finds only a comment mention of 'O_EXCL-style' at line 275. The file-writing path (write_blob_atomic, lines 278-307) uses g_mkstemp (glib), write/fsync/close/unlink (unistd.h, included line 23), and rename (stdio.h). Nothing from fcntl.h is referenced.
findings.safety: Removing an include that contributes no used declarations cannot change the compiled object; a successful recompile proves no hidden dependency.
findings.verify_with: make -C qemu_plugin compiles clean with -Wall -Wextra; tests/plugin/test_plugin_atomic_write_mkstemp.sh exercises the write path.

findings.title: Unreachable kind guard in on_handoff_boundary; marker mode registers permanently no-op exec callbacks on EXIT markers
findings.detail: on_handoff_boundary (line 556) is registered only in pc_mode (line 632), and its HandoffSite is always created with kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER (line 629), so the guard at line 559 can never fire. Relatedly, marker mode registers on_handoff for ANY matched marker kind (lines 646-653: hybrid_match_handoff_insn yields ENTER or EXIT per insn_match.h lines 24-29), and on_handoff (line 546) filters EXIT forever - QEMU1 exits(200) at the ENTER marker before any EXIT marker retires, so the EXIT-site registration plus its heap-allocated site is pure dead weight. Filtering to kind == ENTER at translation time removes both, keeping only on_handoff's guard if desired for the both-markers-in-one-TB case (which the ENTER-only registration still handles correctly, since the ENTER callback exits the process first).
findings.safety: Exec callbacks never modify guest state; the EXIT-site callback body is a no-op today and the ENTER drain semantics are untouched, so drained state files and exit codes are identical in all three trigger modes.
findings.verify_with: scripts/run_e2e.sh (marker mode default) plus MODE=marker and tests/plugin/test_plugin_pc_trigger_resume_pc.sh for pc mode; tests/plugin/test_plugin_oracle_exit_drain.sh confirms oracle mode (which handles EXIT separately) is unaffected.

findings.title: Base M-mode CSR name list hand-maintained in 3 parallel copies while the v3/v4 blocks already use X-macros for the identical pattern
findings.detail: The 13 base M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp) are written out three times: VcpuRegs handle fields (lines 36-48), resolve_handles find_reg calls (lines 187-199), and drain_state_into reads (lines 344-356). The same triplication covers mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl (lines 53-54, 201-202, 360-361) and the 7 V scalar CSRs (lines 75-81, 234-240, 405-411). In every copy the VcpuRegs field name, the gdb lookup string, and the hybrid_state_v1 field name are the same identifier, which is exactly the shape the file already handles with HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST / HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST (lines 58-61, 207-209, 368-372): one line per CSR, three consumers generated. A plugin-local X-macro (e.g. #define BASE_CSR_LIST(X) X(mstatus) X(mepc) ...) collapses 3x22 hand-kept lines into one list and removes the add-a-CSR-touch-3-places drift risk. The shared ABI struct keeps its plain fields - no submodule change needed.
findings.safety: Purely mechanical token generation: the macro expands to the identical find_reg(regs, "name") and s.name = read_reg64(v->name) statements in the same order, and gdbstub register reads have no side effects, so the drained state file is byte-identical.
findings.verify_with: Hybrid e2e with --verify (state_diff compares every transported CSR field), e.g. FILTER=rt_csr_survival scripts/run_e2e.sh, plus tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh; optionally diff the drained state file of one fixture before/after the change.
